original_value: In this paper we aim to show a proof-of-principle approach to detect and monitor weed management using glyphosate-based herbicides in agricultural practices. In a case study in Germany, we demonstrate the application of Sentinel-2 multispectral time-series data. Spectral broadband vegetation indices were analysed to observe vegetation traits and weed damage arising from herbicide-based management. The approach has been validated with stakeholder information about herbicide treatment using commercial products. As a result, broadband NDVI calculated from Sentinel-2 data showed explicit feedback after the glyphosate-based herbicide treatment. Vegetation damage could be detected after just two days following of glyphosate-based herbicide treatment. This trend was observed in three different application scenarios, i.e., during growing stage, before harvest and after harvest. The findings of the study demonstrate the feasibility of satellite based broadband NDVI data for the detection of glyphosate-based herbicide treatment and, e.g., the monitoring of latency to harvesting. The presented results can be used to implement monitoring concepts to provide the necessary transparency about weed treatment in agricultural practices and to support environmental monitoring.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a proof-of-principle method for detecting and monitoring weed management in agricultural practice through the use of glyphosate-based herbicides. A case study in Germany demonstrates how Sentinel-2 multispectral time-series data can be applied. Spectral broadband vegetation indices were evaluated to track vegetation characteristics and herbicide-induced weed damage. The approach was validated using stakeholder information on herbicide treatments with commercial products. The results showed that broadband NDVI derived from Sentinel-2 data responded clearly after glyphosate-based herbicide application. Vegetation damage was detectable just two days after treatment. This pattern appeared in three application scenarios: during the growing stage, before harvest, and after harvest. The study shows that satellite-based broadband NDVI data can feasibly detect glyphosate-based herbicide treatment and, for example, monitor latency to harvesting. These results may help implement monitoring concepts that provide needed transparency about weed treatment in agricultural practice and support environmental monitoring.
